proof:
Source: step 1 (geometry of one graph) and the Lipschitz image bound used in step 4 of the parent proof (step B6 (iii)–(iv) of the proof of Simon 8.5.9), specialised to a single graph piece A; no closedness or measurability of A is used. Notation: H^n := μHE[n] (Mathlib's Euclidean Hausdorff measure on ℝ^N = Euclidean N, an outer measure, so H^n(S) is defined for every set S); p := Grassmannian.project P, the orthogonal projection onto the n-plane P.plane = range p; it is linear (p = P.projectionLinearMap), symmetric (Grassmannian.projectionLinearMap_isSymmetric) and idempotent (Grassmannian.project_project). A set S ⊆ ℝ^N is an L-Lipschitz graph over P when |(y − z) − p(y − z)| ≤ L|p(y − z)| for all y, z ∈ S; every subset of such a set is again one.

1. Pythagoras for p. For v ∈ ℝ^N, symmetry and idempotence give ⟨p v, p v⟩ = ⟨p(p v), v⟩ = ⟨p v, v⟩, hence ⟨p v, v − p v⟩ = 0 and, expanding |p v + (v − p v)|² (norm_add_sq_real), |v|² = |p v|² + |v − p v|².

2. Inverse-Lipschitz estimate on A. Let y, z ∈ A and v := y − z, so p v = p(y) − p(z) by linearity. The hypothesis gives 0 ≤ |v − p v| ≤ L|p v|, hence |v − p v|² ≤ L²|p v|², and by step 1 |y − z|² = |p v|² + |v − p v|² ≤ (1 + L²)|p(y) − p(z)|². Taking square roots, |y − z| ≤ (1 + L²)^{1/2} |p(y) − p(z)|.

3. Injectivity and the inverse map. If y, z ∈ A and p(y) = p(z), step 2 gives |y − z| ≤ 0, so y = z: p is injective on A. Let h := Function.invFunOn p A. By injectivity h(p(y)) = y for every y ∈ A (Set.InjOn.leftInvOn_invFunOn), and therefore h(p(A)) = A (Set.LeftInvOn.image_image).

4. h is K-Lipschitz on p(A) with K := (1 + L²)^{1/2} (as an element of ℝ≥0: Real.toNNReal √(1 + L²)). Indeed, for a = p(y) and b = p(z) with y, z ∈ A, step 3 gives h(a) = y, h(b) = z, so by step 2 dist(h(a), h(b)) = |y − z| ≤ K|p(y) − p(z)| = K·dist(a, b) (LipschitzOnWith.of_dist_le_mul).

5. Lipschitz image bound. By Mathlib's LipschitzOnWith.hausdorffMeasure_image_le (exponent d = n ≥ 0) applied to h on p(A), μH[n](h(p(A))) ≤ K^n·μH[n](p(A)); by step 3 the left side is μH[n](A). In [0, ∞], K^n = (ofReal √(1 + L²))^(n:ℝ) = ofReal(√(1 + L²)^(n:ℝ)) = ofReal((1 + L²)^{n/2}) (ENNReal.ofReal_rpow_of_nonneg, Real.sqrt_eq_rpow, Real.rpow_mul). So μH[n](A) ≤ ofReal((1 + L²)^{n/2})·μH[n](p(A)).

6. Normalisation. By definition μHE[n] = c·μH[n] with the constant c = addHaarScalarFactor volume μH[n] (Measure.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_def, Measure.smul_apply). Multiplying the inequality of step 5 by c gives H^n(A) = c·μH[n](A) ≤ c·ofReal((1 + L²)^{n/2})·μH[n](p(A)) = ofReal((1 + L²)^{n/2})·H^n(p(A)). ∎
key_steps: Pythagoras for the orthogonal projection: |v|² = |p v|² + |v − p v|².
Graph inequality ⇒ |y − z| ≤ (1 + L²)^{1/2}|p(y) − p(z)| on A; hence p is injective on A.
h := invFunOn p A satisfies h(p(A)) = A and is (1 + L²)^{1/2}-Lipschitz on p(A).
μHE[n] = c·μH[n] transfers the bound to H^n.
